title: The frequency below which no electron escapes
spoken: The threshold frequency equals the escape work divided by h.
explanation: Setting the largest kinetic energy to zero gives the frequency whose quantum only just pays the escape work. Below it the model emits nothing, however bright the light.
assumptions: One electron receives the whole of one quantum, h times the frequency, and nothing from a second quantum.
Escaping costs the electron at least the escape work; any further loss on the way out is not negative.
These are modern teaching equations in SI notation, not a transcription of the printed section 8.

notes.title: Threshold frequency
notes.explanation: The lowest frequency at which one quantum can free an electron. It depends on the metal, through the escape work, and on nothing about the light but its frequency.

notes.title: Escape work
notes.explanation: The same escape work as in the energy budget. A metal that holds its electrons more tightly has a higher threshold.

notes.title: Planck's constant
notes.explanation: Dividing an energy by h turns it into the frequency whose quantum carries that energy.

notes.title: Where the budget reaches zero
notes.explanation: Put zero for the largest kinetic energy in the budget and solve for the frequency. This threshold is a consequence of the one-quantum assumption, not an independent measurement of it.
